column4: CHECK: The abi change-log paragraph of the spec is the only change log for rx_info.abi, and a bump updates that paragraph in the bump's own commit.
rx_info.abi is 71 on every artifact.
Every artifact of both engines carries a <PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES stamp line directly after <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES is the artifact's CPU-guarded byte count.
<PREFIX>_SIMD_GUARDED_BYTES reads 0ULL on every artifact, since no SIMD form exists and -fmemfn-simd is inert.
CHECK: Every length decision reads the SIMD-off length (len_uncut minus the guarded bytes; the size caps' measure minus the guarded text's), which equals the plain length wherever nothing is guarded.
CHECK: Each offset-skip/pre-check function (<prefix>_reqrun, <prefix>_reqrun_whole, <prefix>_ofsskip) keeps its loop under the head <prefix>_<fn>__body, and the function itself is one call to it.
CHECK: The forwarding body of those functions has the form return <prefix>_<fn>__body(subject, n, pos[, tables]); the SIMD-off shape that a CPU-guarded helper adds #if arms above.
CHECK: <prefix>_reqrun, <prefix>_reqrun_whole and <prefix>_ofsskip (and their __body heads) are static inline in the .c, so no linked symbol is involved.
CHECK: A ${...} pattern's <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL reads "selected" rather than "declined-nullable-default" (its variable, not a nullability decline, turns the prefilter off).
CHECK: A collapse rung is not offered on an attempt the collapse cannot help (no collapsible repeat; nullable but not empty_admits).
CHECK: When a compile drops the prefilter for size, <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY's "size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP" figure is the exact artifact's size, not a wasted retry's.
CHECK: The --emit-ir prefilter vocabulary includes the values no-variable and no-size-cap (ir_listing.md).
CHECK: Both prefilter declines read the E1 fact empty_admits instead of bare nullability.

CHECK: A nullable pattern whose every empty path crosses a non-multiline ^/\A AND $/\Z/\z keeps its exact hybrid prefilter; its ENGINE_SEL reads "selected" and VM_PREFILTER "hybrid" with prefilter tables, scan and VM_PREFILTER_LANG present.
CHECK: A near-miss that exhausts the step budget answers nomatch (K65's direction).

CHECK: The five in-loop ADVANCE sites (DFA stay skips fwd/rev, scan-edge loops unbounded/counted both directions, VM span scan) are spelled while ((MORE)[ && CNT < NULL] && (MEMBER)) { with the step and counter increment on their own lines in a braced body.
CHECK: In those ADVANCE loops the counter cap is written as %lluULL.
CHECK: Possessify arm A values a context gate (\b, \B, a one-character lookaround) in a quantifier's follow by what it can admit next; arm B reads a backreference's FIRST from its groups.
Every VM artifact carries <PREFIX>_VM_POSS_ARMS (section 6.3), 0x0u where no arm was needed.
CHECK: -fno-poss-ctx-follow -fno-poss-bref-first restores the abi-65 possessify program apart from the abi digits and the VM_POSS_ARMS stamp line.
CHECK: A possessify route flip can move RX_ENGINE itself (\w++\b is discharged and DFA-routed).
rx_info.flags' strategy mask is derived from src/core/axes.def: it masks every axis bit except the named kept set (tuning.md section 2, THE rx_info.flags RULE).
-fno-size-term (bit 18) and -fno-scan-edge (bit 21) are masked out of rx_info.flags.
A future axis bit is masked out of rx_info.flags on arrival unless it is in the named kept set.
CHECK: The DFA-route candidate table has rows first-memchr-bounded and first-class-bounded; RX_DFA_PREFILTER and rx_info.prefilter carry those two values (tuning.md 2.42, 6.3).

CHECK: On a seeded forward DFA scan whose start set S cannot match empty and is a proper subset of the start state's escape set E, the bounded skip tests S instead of E (one byte by memchr, several by a 256-entry <prefix>_start_bytes table) and re-seeds the scan state from the byte before its landing where it moved.
CHECK: A VM hybrid's inlined prefilter takes the first-memchr-bounded/first-class-bounded start-set skip too; -fno-start-set disables both the DFA and the VM start-set hats.
Every artifact of both engines carries <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS and <PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC stamp lines directly after <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS reads "none" on every artifact until the kit's first SIMD-on form.
<PREFIX>_MEMFN_LIBC is the artifact's source-level inventory of C library calls, or "none".
The <PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS and _MEMFN_LIBC lines render before the emitted-size measurement, so a size-cap retry's quoted size (<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY) of its discarded attempt includes them.

CHECK: The VM-route start-set row first-class applies to a VM artifact with no DFA prefilter, an unanchored pattern, and a start_set fact S that cannot match empty and has fewer than 256 members; it seeks the next byte of S (a 256-entry table) before the first attempt and after each failed one.
The VM start-set seek sits after the range guard, K50, rx_valid_upto and the K65/K66 pre-check, so a pre-check NOMATCH and a PCREC_ERR_UTF are unchanged.
Every artifact of both engines carries <PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN, which reads "first-class" or "none" (section 6.3).
-fno-start-set (bit 47) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
CHECK: A give-up that the start-set-skipped attempts would have hit may become the answer (section 3.1).

Axis req-use (tuning.md 2.41, listed by --list-axes) is a two-row first-match table deciding what a search body does with an emitted run pre-check's answer; its handoff row keeps the pre-check's first window hit c.
The run pre-check's first window hit c is the LEFTMOST occurrence at or after startpos, a written contract of the search block.

With the handoff row the body begins its scan at max(startpos, c - K), K the window's maximum BYTE offset from the attempt start (core fact req_run_maxoff in --emit-facts), rounded up to a character start under a multibyte encoding, only when it moved.

The three bodies with a DFA scan (DFA unanchored scan and its seed, DFA attempt loop's first start, VM hybrid's first prefilter call) read the handoff at their one start site; \G keeps reading startpos.
Every artifact of both engines carries <PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF, which is "<K>" or "none" (section 6.3).
-fno-req-handoff (bit 46) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
CHECK: The whole-window pre-check admission (tuning.md 2.29) is a first-match row table none / one-attempt / dominated / set-leads / emitted, listed by --list-axes as axis req-admit.

CHECK: The set-leads row emits the necessary SET's pick's one-byte check in front of the run search where that byte is strictly rarer than the run's scan member (a tie keeps the run alone); on the no-DFA-scan VM route the K65 whole-set half then skips that byte.
-fno-req-set-lead (bit 45) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
pcrec_find_pick's NONE answer is the argmin of MASS's uniform mass (cardinality), ties to the reader's rightmost (findings.md section 4).
CHECK: Under NONE (every -e utf8 artifact under the default analysis) a masked run scans an EXACT position before a two-member pair.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY keeps its four tokens; a set-leads artifact reads "emitted".

CHECK: The necessary-run analysis (src/facts/req.c) admits, beside a single byte, a POSITION whose byte set is one two-member cube (T, K), such as a caseless letter [Ss], [jk] or an alternation's one-bit hull.

CHECK: Necessary runs are ranked by information (sum of popcount(K)) and floored at PCREC_MIN_REQ_RUN_BITS (16); an alternation's common head and tail are taken as the cube hull of its branches (tuning.md 2.28, 2.39).

CHECK: For an artifact whose req_run is masked, the run pre-check blocks (<prefix>_reqrun, and on the no-DFA-scan VM route <prefix>_reqrun_whole) compare the run masked through the run compare's words row, e.g. (<prefix>_w4(subject + cand) & <prefix>_w4("\337\337\337\337")) == <prefix>_w4("SELE"); the bytes row under -fno-run-overlap.
CHECK: A run block whose scan member is a pair scans both members as two memchr streams leapfrogged inside its one guarded loop.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN gains a /mask suffix when the run is masked (section 6.3).
CHECK: <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE becomes the set's pick where the run's scan member is a pair; <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY may read "emitted" with <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "none".
CHECK: The K65 whole-set half tests every set member that the run's EXACT positions do not prove.
-fno-req-run-fold (bit 44) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
Every masked run position is canonical (T & ~K == 0, popcount(K) 7 or 8); the compiler refuses a non-canonical position as an internal error.
Every search of the pair arm sits inside the block's while (pos + maxk < n) guard.
A run pin covers exact positions only, so no masked run enters dfa_pfs[].

Every literal-run compare in emitted C (offset-skip block's run term, the run pre-check's compare, the VM's literal run, the island's single-child chains) is written by ONE emitter function with a first-match row table (src/gen/runcmp.c, tuning.md 2.38).
An EXACT run of length 3, 5-7 or 9-15 takes the overlap row: two overlapping natural-width words, the last at offset L - W.

Each overlap-row word is loaded by a static inline uint<8W>_t <prefix>_w<W>(const void *) memcpy helper and compared against the same load of a string literal, the compares joined by && in offset order.
Every run length other than 3, 5-7, 9-15 keeps the constant-length memcmp byte for byte.
The <prefix>_w<W> helpers are emitted only where an artifact writes a word row, once each, ahead of their first use.
Every artifact of both engines carries <PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS (section 6.3), a count of the compares the overlap row wrote, emitted after the engine body.
-fno-run-overlap (bit 43) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
Every overlap-row word lies inside the run (o + W <= L).
Each overlap-row word's constant is a string literal, never an integer literal of the target's byte order.
The overlap-row compare reads exactly the bytes the caller's existing bounds guard covers.

CHECK: The scan edge (tuning.md 2.18) takes a chain whose members carry only an END (\z) view on the forward and anchored machines, since the scan's own stop at n evaluates it; and on any machine a chain whose head is another state's view target, which starts one state later (tuning.md 2.37, -fno-view-edge).
<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED has the value "anchored" (section 6.3, tuning.md 2.35).

CHECK: A hybrid whose <PREFIX>_VM_START is not "unanchored" reads VM_RESEED "anchored", takes the pre-abi-49 retry, and emits no adaptive tail or its two per-call locals; its C equals its -fno-hyb-reseed artifact's byte for byte.
A DFA artifact whose <PREFIX>_NCAPS is 2 or more promises groups that no match can set (reached only through a subroutine call, or under {0}), and <prefix>_search reports them as PCREC_UNSET.
On a DFA artifact the dead-group fill is emitted on each success path (reverse-pass and pinned unanchored forms, per-start attempt form), after the caps[0] write and before return 1.
A no-match (and startpos > n) on a DFA artifact returns 0 with caps untouched, including caps[1..NCAPS-1].
The VM, the VM hybrid, the anchored _match_caps entries and the _in spellings leave caps untouched on every non-success return (checked by tests/codegen/run_nomatch_caps.sh).
The shared block's guard carries the abi as its value, #define PCREC_RX_ABI_H <abi>, and the block opens with #if defined(PCREC_RX_ABI_H) && (PCREC_RX_ABI_H + 0) != <abi> followed by #error.
A translation unit that includes artifacts of two different abis fails to compile, with an #error naming the cause.
Same-abi artifacts in one translation unit: the first shared block wins and every later one is skipped.
CHECK: The + 0 makes the test refuse a pre-54 artifact included FIRST (its guard is defined empty); a pre-54 artifact included AFTER a 54+ one is the one order that stays silent.
The compiler emits every artifact under a fixed two-byte placeholder prefix and writes the caller's -p spelling only onto the finished text.
Every size-predicated selection (VM entry shape, size term's trigger and ladder, emitted-size caps) is decided on the text at a canonical prefix length (limits.md Size limits and the prefix).
The same pattern under the same options gets the same artifact whatever its prefix, differing only in spelling.
<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES reports the canonical (placeholder-prefix) length, not the prefix's own length.
rx_info.name's default is the prefix.
CHECK: A DFA scan edge asks src/gen/clskit.c's class-form table at the scan site and writes the answer through the emitters a VM class read uses (tuning.md 2.18).
CHECK: A scan edge over a byte range not starting at 0 is spelled (unsigned)(b - lo) <= span u, the VM's spelling.
CHECK: A VM artifact whose class is a range from 0 is spelled b <= hi.
CHECK: At --tune=-2/-1 a scan edge's ASCII case pair is the fold compare (<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold", section 6.3).
CHECK: At --tune=-2/-1 a byte class takes its kit matcher only where the kit, written once per read, is smaller than the table its site reads (byte-kit, tuning.md 2.33).
CHECK: A byte kit whose set spans 0..255 carries no always-false bound.

CHECK: Axis I (the scan edge's run-extension body) has a third object kit: at --tune=-2/-1 an edge whose class is on the class-form table's byte-kit row (not one interval, not an ASCII fold pair) tests its run with a file-scope static inline <prefix>_<machine>_scankit<N> instead of a 256-byte table.
<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE has the value "kit" (section 6.3).
CHECK: No artifact at --tune 0/+1/+2 uses the scan-edge kit body; -fno-cls-kit restores the table body.
CHECK: The VM's per-class byte shape classifier is the first-match class-form table in src/gen/clskit.c (tuning.md 2.33, 5.4's lambda row).

CHECK: At --tune=-2/-1 a VM byte class that is neither one interval nor an ASCII fold pair is tested by a static inline <prefix>_class_kit<N> in place of a 32-byte bitmap (unless the artifact takes the shared atom table).
<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT counts the byte-class kit matchers too (section 6.3).
CHECK: At --tune 0/+1/+2 a VM byte class's test is the bitmap/compare form, not the kit.
CHECK: At every tune position a WIDE class whose set is one interval of code points at or below U+00FF (-e utf8 [\x{e0}-\x{ff}]) is one range compare.
Every artifact's shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block has #define PCREC_ERR_UTF (-9) (section 4).
Every artifact carries the <PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK stamp (section 6.3).
Every artifact exports the <prefix>_valid_upto entry with its declaration (section 3.1.2).
Every artifact carries the .c-only macro <prefix>_VALID_LB, which the body of <prefix>_valid_upto reads.
A -e utf8 artifact carrying a ${name} variable has its <prefix>_var_valid re-spelled on the <prefix>_valid_upto entry (one validator).
A -futf-check artifact under -e utf8 has one precheck line at each entry's caller-position site (section 3.1).
A -fstartpos-guard=align artifact under -e utf8 carries the alignment in place of the K50 refusal, and its <PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD reads "align".
PCREC_FORCE_UTF_CHECK is bit 39 and PCREC_FORCE_STARTPOS_ALIGN is bit 40.
PCREC_FORCE_UTF_CHECK and PCREC_FORCE_STARTPOS_ALIGN are CONTRACT bits: kept in rx_info.flags, masked only under byte.
Under byte, PCREC_FORCE_UTF_CHECK and PCREC_FORCE_STARTPOS_ALIGN are inert and a byte artifact is byte-identical under either.

A VM hybrid whose prefilter answers for a LARGER language than the pattern's (a lookaround or atomic cut erased, or the [OPT-4] count collapse) retries after a failed attempt by either stepping or asking the prefilter again, chosen per CALL from the gaps the prefilter's own answers jump (tuning.md 2.35).
An exact-language hybrid and a clamped (MRL clamp) hybrid keep the non-adaptive retry.
Every hybrid artifact carries <PREFIX>_VM_RESEED naming the row that fired (section 6.3); a non-hybrid artifact has no such effect.
The adaptive retry runs a subset of the attempts the non-adaptive retry ran, so a call that gave up (PCREC_ERR_STEPS/_WORK) under a budget can now answer, and never the reverse.
-fno-hyb-reseed (PCREC_NO_HYB_RESEED, bit 37) is masked out of rx_info.flags.

CHECK: A class with more than one member, some member of which encodes deeper than one code unit (-e utf8: \p{L}, [^a], ., [e-u with diaeresis range]), is tested by a VM program as <prefix>_decode followed by <prefix>_wcls<N>.
<prefix>_wcls<N> is a static inline function whose form the --tune class table picks (section 5.4's lambda row).
<prefix>_decode is a static inline encoding-seam entry, declared nowhere, emitted ahead of the program.
The utf8 caseless span compare calls <prefix>_decode rather than carrying a private decoder.
Every VM artifact carries a <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT line (section 6.3).
Wide classes that refused on the VM's code cap compile now: \P{Unknown} under --engine=vm (K55) and the K53 sets under --engine=vm.
-fno-cls-kit (PCREC_NO_CLS_KIT, bit 36) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
-fno-cls-kit denies the whole kit, the shared atom table included.

A VM program whose table-reading byte classes (no singleton, range or fold-pair compare covers them) number at least 11, and whose byte partition has at most 64 atoms, emits ONE static const unsigned char <prefix>_class_atoms[256].

For each such class the atom-table program emits one static inline matcher <prefix>_class_atom<N> (one load, one shift of a 64-bit immediate) in place of a <prefix>_class_bitmap<N>[32], and the program calls the matcher where it read the bitmap (tuning.md 2.34).
Every VM artifact carries a <PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS line (section 6.3).
The atom table is selected after the entry rung, so the program length the rung's knee compares is unchanged.
-fno-cls-pack (PCREC_NO_CLS_PACK, bit 38) is masked out of rx_info.flags and denies the atom row alone.

CHECK: Under an encoding restricting where a match may begin (utf8), a NULLABLE pattern's unanchored DFA scan (DFA artifact entry and VM hybrid's internal prefilter) seeks search_from past leading continuation bytes at offset 0.
CHECK: Under utf8 a NULLABLE pattern's ENG_ATTEMPT start loop skips offset 0 and the VM seeks its first attempt_position.
CHECK: Under utf8 the anchored match-here bodies of a NULLABLE pattern answer -1 at a non-boundary offset 0 (section 3.1's two bullets).
A non-nullable pattern gains none of the offset-0 start rule, since a match that consumes a byte already begins on a character start ([K50-NULLGATE]).
The DFA's "unwrapped" <prefix>_match (section 3.2) carries the [K50] caller-startpos guard and refuses a mid-character ctx->pos.
Answers move only on subjects that begin with a continuation byte (to libpcre2's) and on mid-character ctx->pos at the unwrapped DFA _match (to the refusal).

CHECK: A lookaround whose body's language is a set of single byte-expressible characters ((?<=\$), (?!y), (?=[ab]), non-atomic and alpha spellings) is lowered to the same context node \b/\B build (tuning.md 2.32, T3).
CHECK: A context node is carried by the DFA on its class axis and tested by the VM as one guarded byte read, so a pattern whose only DFA-excluding construct was such a lookaround gets a DFA artifact.
UCP \b/\B under -e byte compile (the Latin-1 word set is byte-expressible).
-fno-ctx-node (PCREC_NO_CTX_NODE, bit 35) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
CHECK: Under --features all every module's name joins PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES, emitted scaffolding regardless of whether the caller asked for the module; module ucp is (*UCP), --ucp, flags u.
CHECK: Stamps keep the requested feature set.

CHECK: The necessary run's scan-member pick (pcrec_find_run_scan_index, src/core/findings.c) orders candidates [n-1, n-2, ..., 0] so a data tie goes to the run's positional rightmost tied member, matching the reader's NONE answer.
CHECK: pcrec_find_run_window_start (the window MASS rule) ties leftmost, matching its own NONE.
CHECK: <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN's @idx and on some artifacts its window offset move with the pick (the truncation window is re-derived around the pick's member).
Choosing which necessary run/set member is scanned moves only a speed, never an answer, since every byte of a necessary run or set is necessary.
CHECK: pcrec_lit_run (src/core/cpset.c) requires a run of THREE or more consecutive one-byte literals; a two-byte pair falls through to the per-element byte chain; no deny flag.
CHECK: pcrec_lit_run is the one node-grain fact the VM's chain emission, cost walk and slot walk all share.
CHECK: <PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS counts the run compares written, and a VM artifact whose only lit-run sites were two-byte runs loses that count.
No answer and no give-up moves with the literal-run compare: it accepts exactly the bytes the chain accepted, and step, work and node budgets charge what the chain charged (limits.md 3.1).
The island's single-child trie chain is a different mechanism sharing only the P4 primitive, and is not subject to the three-byte floor.
A subroutine call is nullable iff its callee's minimum width is 0 (u.call.minw's least fixpoint, published by the call graph before the pattern-facts E1 seal).
A quantifier over a non-nullable callee (e.g. (a|(?1))*?b) carries no empty-iteration guard; its slot legend and <PREFIX>_NSLOTS have no <PREFIX>_SLOT_EMPTY_GUARD<n> entry.
A callee that is nullable, directly or through another call, keeps its empty-iteration guard.
The E1 nullable fact (--emit-facts) is unaffected by the least-fixpoint rule for call nullability.

CHECK: In a VM program, three or more (originally two or more) consecutive one-byte literals on one concatenation are consumed under ONE label by one bounds check and one constant-length compare: if (scan_position + L <= subject_length && !memcmp(subject + scan_position, "<run>", L)).
An alternation island's single-child trie chain is the same run compare at its node's depth (tuning.md 2.31).
The artifact gains #include <string.h> where nothing else in it needed one.
EVERY VM artifact (a hybrid included) carries <PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS, the count of run compares written (section 6.3).
-fno-lit-run (PCREC_NO_LIT_RUN, bit 33) is masked out of rx_info.flags.
The --emit-ir listing has a compare op (ir_listing.md).
Every artifact of both engines carries <PREFIX>_FINDINGS (section 6), written beside the rx_info definition.
rx_info has an APPENDED member findings (section 6) with its initializer line.

The byte-frequency prior (necessary-byte pick, run scan member and window, G1's density rule, offset-k selection) is DATA from src/findings/default.rxt (docs/spec/findings.md); the shipped default normalizes to the old table exactly.
CHECK: The offset-k selection's rate read takes the encoding gate the data declares, so under -e utf8 (where the default declares nothing) it ranks offset sets by CARDINALITY, MASS's NONE answer.
The rate chooses cost only: every set the offset-k selection ranks is necessary (findings design 6.2a).
PCREC_NO_VM_ANCHOR_BOUND, PCREC_NO_END_WINDOW and PCREC_NO_REQ_BYTE (bits 28-30) are masked out of rx_info.flags.
rx_info.flags records the request with testing/tuning denials masked OUT, because an axis that changes no answer must not make two identically-behaving artifacts differ in their reflection surface.

CHECK: The necessary RUN's scan member (rn_scan_index in src/opt/reqbyte.c) is the RIGHTMOST member under every encoding whose byte-frequency prior is not keyed to (all but byte), matching rb_pick's !bytekey fallback.
byte-encoding artifacts are untouched by the !bytekey rightmost rule: !bytekey gates the whole candidate difference.

CHECK: The run pre-check's scan loop (and K66's whole-run loop where the route emits one) is a file-scope static inline size_t <prefix>_reqrun / <prefix>_reqrun_whole(subject, n, pos) written by the SAME emitter as the <prefix>_ofsskip prefilter block.
<prefix>_reqrun returns the first position at which the run begins inside [pos, n), or n.
CHECK: The search entry's pre-check is one line per block: if (<prefix>_reqrun(subject, subject_length, search_from) >= subject_length) return 0;.
The block's loop guard pos + L-1 < n is false on an empty window, so its memchr is never reached there (K27's memchr(NULL, c, 0) obligation is discharged by the guard).
The <prefix>_reqrun and <prefix>_reqrun_whole helpers are static and declared nowhere.
-fno-req-run restores the one-byte check; -fno-req-byte removes the whole pre-check mechanism.
CHECK: G1 reads the scan byte of every <prefix>_ofsskip prefilter, not only memchr forms, and elides a RUN pre-check where the prefilter's test verifies the whole run at its pin (tuning.md 2.29).
RX_DFA_PREFILTER has the values "run-pinned" and "run-pinned-bounded" (section 6.3); rx_info.prefilter mirrors them.

CHECK: The run-pinned rows are selected ahead of every other form where the run sits at a fixed offset from every match's start and the scan already runs on its scan member there; the offset-skip block compares the whole run as one constant-length memcmp and its OFFSETS may start 0*.
Axis bit 32 is PCREC_NO_RUN_PREFILTER / -fno-run-prefilter (tuning.md 2.30), masked out of rx_info.flags.
-fno-offset-skip removes the run-pinned prefilter rows too.
CHECK: -fno-run-prefilter restores the pre-S1 artifact on every run-row artifact; the admission elisions have no axis.
PCREC_MAX_REQ_RUN_EMIT is 8: a necessary run longer than it is truncated to the window the frequency prior picks.
On a VM artifact with <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none" the pre-check is the call's only linear NO-MATCH PROOF.

CHECK: A VM artifact with VM_PREFILTER "none" and a run longer than its window follows the window's scan loop with a second scan loop of the same shape comparing the WHOLE run (emit_req_run_rest, src/gen/emit_dfa.c; ReqRun.whole/whole_len/at).
K65's rq_set[] block drops every byte of the whole run; <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN still names the window.
CHECK: -fno-req-run and -fno-req-byte still remove the whole-run compare.

On a VM artifact with <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none" (backreference- or linked-call-bearing patterns on the auto route, and --engine=vm builds without -fprefilter) the necessary-byte pre-check is the call's only linear NO-MATCH proof.

CHECK: After the byte check or the run check such an artifact emits one block: a static const unsigned char rq_set[] of every necessary byte the first half did not test, and a loop memchr-ing each; any absent member answers NOMATCH (emit_req_set_rest, src/gen/emit_dfa.c; Job.req_set).
-fno-req-byte removes the whole necessary-set mechanism (tuning.md 2.29).

CHECK: req_route_one_attempt (src/gen/emit_dfa.c) declines the pre-check on a one-attempt route only if that attempt is LINEAR: an EXACT-language hybrid DFA in front, or a frameless VM program (Job.vm_frameless, published by vm_plan_entry).
A count-collapsed superset hybrid is not a no-match proof; an exact match is.
-fno-req-byte removes the pre-check mechanism on both routes.
Module vars gives a pattern ${name}, whose bytes the CALLER supplies per call.
A fixed-literal ABI type rx_var {name, p, len} is in the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block of every artifact of both engines.
rx_ctx has two APPENDED fields: const rx_var *vars; size_t nvars;.
rx_matchfn's signature is untouched by variables: a var-bearing artifact's <prefix>_match is still an rx_matchfn byte for byte.
#define PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR (-8) is the THIRD below-the-floor code, with PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS's shape: a caller REFUSAL, nothing attempted, caps untouched.
rx_info has two APPENDED members: const char *const *vars; int nvars; (the variable-NAME table, on rx_info.groups' model).
A var-bearing artifact carries <PREFIX>_NVARS and one internal <PREFIX>_VAR_<NAME> index macro per name.

The <PREFIX>_VAR_<NAME> macro is the ARTIFACT's own index into its names table, never something a caller writes: variables are passed BY NAME, because an index is meaningless across separately compiled artifacts.
A var-bearing artifact carries a <prefix>_var_names[] table that rx_info.vars points at.
A var-bearing artifact carries a <prefix>_vars_resolve static that scans the caller's array ONCE PER CALL and evaluates each distinct expansion.

There is no separate compare entry for variables: the encoding seam's pair $_span_match / $_span_match_caseless takes the reference side as a POINTER AND A LENGTH, so ONE pair serves a backreference (subject + start, end - start) and a variable (the caller's resolved value).
Under a multi-byte encoding a fifth encoding-seam entry $_var_valid joins the span-match pair.
Every artifact carrying a backreference has its residual's NAME and signature in the generalised span-match form.
<prefix>_search and its _in siblings take a trailing const rx_var *vars, size_t nvars pair, because they are not rx_ctx-shaped and cannot read the ctx; the descriptor stays LAST (section 10.2).
docs/spec/vars.md is the module vars' own contract page.
Every artifact of both engines carries the shared-prologue stamp <PREFIX>_REQ_WHY, a closed four-token set: "emitted", "none", "one-attempt", "dominated".
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY says whether the artifact acted on what the necessary-byte/run analyses found and, if not, which of two measured declines applies.
<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY is a SEPARATE stamp: the <PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE / <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN pair keeps naming what the ANALYSIS found, so neither value space carries decline information.

Every artifact of both engines carries the shared-prologue stamp <PREFIX>_REQ_RUN.
<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN is the run's bytes as lowercase hex, then @, then the scanned member's index within them, or the token "none" at L < 2.

-fno-req-run restores the byte-check text on the run population; -fno-req-byte removes the pre-check mechanism entirely (tuning.md 2.27-2.28).
The flags enum in lib/pcrec.h is spelled 1ull << N, because PCREC_NO_REQ_RUN is bit 31 and 1u << 32 is undefined behaviour.
pcrec_options.flags is uint64_t.

The essential generated-by line names PCREC_VERSION and the abi on every artifact, whatever -fcomments says: /* Generated by pcrec <PCREC_VERSION> (abi <N>). Pattern: ... */.
PCREC_VERSION (lib/pcrec.h) is a semver string independent of abi: it versions the tool, abi versions one artifact's emitted scaffolding.
pcrec --version prints the PCREC_VERSION string (docs/spec/cli.md).

A default artifact carries no NON-ESSENTIAL comment lines; every comment line leaves every artifact of both engines except the generated-by/pattern-echo provenance line and the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H type block's doc-comments (the ESSENTIAL class, D112).
-fcomments restores the non-essential comments.

The essential generated-by line also carries the abi digit, e.g. /* Generated by pcrec (abi 27). Pattern: ... */ (since extended with PCREC_VERSION).
Every artifact of both engines carries exactly one shared-prologue line #define <PREFIX>_TUNE "<token>", a closed five-token selection stamp.
At the default position balanced the --tune dial moves nothing but the <PREFIX>_TUNE stamp: its row in src/core/tune.c is all em-dash sentinels and its deny mask is empty.
At no --tune position does a struct offset, an rx_info member or an answer move: the dial's acceptance criterion.

On a composed artifact a delivering call site retains what its callee matched.
Composition's effects are invisible on a non-composed compile (an artifact built without --source).
